firstViewportText: Creatine Over-the-counter medicine · Sold without a prescription where approved. A pharmacist or clinician can still be asked. In 10 seconds Does it work? How it works Safety Interactions For someone like me? What to measure Alternatives Unknowns Deep evidence What changed · No reviewed conclusion yet In 10 seconds Over-the-counter medicine · Last evidence check 2026-09-06 · No reviewed conclusion yet What it is Creatine is an over-the-counter medicine. ✓ Verified evidence present § Regulatory label A register records an approval and no prescription-only classification was recorded. US register · 2026-08-28 (recorded source, not a stored snapshot) Why people use it Recorded use, not yet reviewed: Sold as a dietary supplement for strength, power and lean mass. Not approved by the FDA or EMA for any disease. The same molecule is used clinically as metabolite replacement in the inherited cerebral creatine deficiency syndromes. … Awaiting review An older RNAWiki record holds this use statement. No reviewer has signed it, so it is shown as a recorded statement and not as a conclusion. Harris RC, Soderlund K, Hultman E. Elevation of creatine in resting and exercised muscle of normal subjects by creatine supplementation.
